speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether he can provide an update on the number of e-scooter accidents and near-misses in 2017 involving pedestrians on footpaths and walkways; (b) what avenues for redress or compensation are available for pedestrians injured in e-scooter accidents; and (c) how awareness of the relevant laws can be enhanced among e-scooter and electric bicycle users of (i) local and (ii) foreign origin.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will step up efforts to prevent accidents through enforcement and education.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: LTA is working with 800 Active Mobility Patrol volunteers to conduct regular patrols in their communities and also to share safe riding practices.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: LTA will soon be conducting a campaign to raise awareness of the active mobility rules and penalties.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The Safe Riding Programme will be launched in schools, foreign worker dormitories and community centres.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It will be compulsory for all cyclists and PMD users who are caught riding recklessly.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In the event of an accident, the victim should file a Police report, and the Police will investigate.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If the offender is convicted in Court for committing an offence, the Court will consider if compensation to the victim should be paid.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The victim can also seek compensation through civil lawsuits, mediation or private settlement.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: All types of bicycles, including power-assisted bicycles or e-bikes, are not allowed to be used on expressways.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The use of PMDs on all public roads is also prohibited.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Repeat offenders will face stiffer penalties, including Court action.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The reason I raise this is because some of my residents are worried that when an accident occurs, there could be a double financial tragedy.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The injured party is injured, has medical bills, the person riding the device may be of limited means and unable to provide compensation even if the Civil Court finds him or her liable.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have now almost a year of experience and, in the light of that experience, we should see what other rules we should introduce, rules we should tweak or toughen.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have started registering e-bikes, so whether there is a case to also register e-scooters.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I do not think we should be registering all scooters or all bicycles but I think those which are power-assisted and, therefore, potentially can incur greater harm, there may be a case of some sort of registration.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I leave it to the panel to review this.
